# fontpixel Python API reference

<!-- Generated by tools/bindings/gen_pyref.py; do not edit by hand. -->

Every public module, class, function, method, property and constant of the
`fontpixel` package with its typed signature (as in the bundled type stubs) and
docstring. Plain-data shapes (`FontMetrics`, `RenderOptions`, `PcfWriteOptions`,
...) are the `TypedDict`s and `Literal` aliases of `fontpixel.types`; see
[python-api.md](python-api.md) for the concepts and how to discover option
shapes at run time.

## fontpixel

fontpixel: bitmap font toolkit (Python bindings).

The complete native API lives in this package; ``fontpixel.compat.bdfparser``
provides a bdfparser-compatible layer on the same Rust core.

### `fontpixel.AmbiguousFormatError(FontpixelError)`

*exception* -- Several formats match; pass an explicit format.

### `fontpixel.BdfParseError(FontpixelError)`

*exception* -- Fatal BDF syntax error.

### `fontpixel.Bitmap(width: int = ..., height: int = ..., depth: Depth = ..., limits: BitmapLimits | None = ...) -> Bitmap`

*class*

A Mono or Gray8 raster (`fontpixel::model::GlyphBitmap`). Always owned:
reading a glyph's bitmap returns a copy; assign it back to edit the glyph.

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.as_bytes() -> bytes`

*method* -- A copy of the canonical storage (`Bitmap::as_bytes`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.bbox() -> Bounds`

*method*

Tight ink rectangle in bottom-left coordinates, as a bounds dict
(`Bitmap::bbox`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.bold(n: int = ...) -> Bitmap`

*method* -- Rightward emboldening by `n` pixels (`Bitmap::bold`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.byte_pad(pixels: int) -> Bitmap`

*method* -- Pad the width up to a multiple of `pixels` (`Bitmap::byte_pad`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.composite(source: BitmapLike, x: int = ..., y: int = ..., mode: CompositeMode | None = ...) -> None`

*method*

Combine `source` into this bitmap in place at `(x, y)` with `mode`
(`Bitmap::composite`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.composite_region(source: BitmapLike, region: Bounds, x: int = ..., y: int = ..., mode: CompositeMode | None = ...) -> None`

*method*

Combine `region` (bounds dict, top-left offsets into `source`) of
`source` in place at `(x, y)` (`Bitmap::composite_region`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.concat(other: BitmapLike, direction: Direction | None = ..., alignment: Alignment | None = ..., gap: int = ...) -> Bitmap`

*method*

Concatenate with `other` (`Bitmap::concat`). The later operand wins
where both have ink.

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.concat_all(bitmaps: Iterable[BitmapLike], direction: Direction | None = ..., alignment: Alignment | None = ..., gaps: Sequence[int] | None = ..., limits: BitmapLimits | None = ...) -> Bitmap`

*static method*

Concatenate several bitmaps in one allocation (`Bitmap::concat_all`).
`gaps` is empty or has one entry per boundary.

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.copy() -> Bitmap`

*method* -- An independent copy.

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.crop(width: int, height: int, x: int = ..., y: int = ...) -> Bitmap`

*method*

Crop or zero-extend to `width`×`height` at bottom-left offset `(x, y)`
(`Bitmap::crop`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.crop_bounds(bounds: Bounds) -> Bitmap`

*method*

Crop to a bounds dict `{width, height, x, y}` (`Bitmap::crop_bounds`;
also `GlyphBitmap::crop`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.depth: Depth`

*property* -- `"mono"` or `"gray8"`.

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.enlarge(x: int, y: int | None = ...) -> Bitmap`

*method* -- Scale by integer factors (`Bitmap::enlarge`; `y` defaults to `x`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.extend(left: int = ..., right: int = ..., top: int = ..., bottom: int = ...) -> Bitmap`

*method* -- Add blank margins (`Bitmap::extend`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.flip_horizontal() -> Bitmap`

*method* -- Mirror left/right (`Bitmap::flip_horizontal`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.flip_vertical() -> Bitmap`

*method* -- Mirror top/bottom (`Bitmap::flip_vertical`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.from_bytes(width: int, height: int, data: Buffer | Sequence[int], layout: ByteLayout | None = ..., depth: Depth = ..., limits: BitmapLimits | None = ...) -> Bitmap`

*static method*

From an exact-sized byte stream in `layout` (a `ByteLayout` dict:
`bit_order` "msb"/"lsb", `byte_order` "big"/"little", `row_alignment`,
`scan_unit`, `row_order` "top-down"/"bottom-up") (`Bitmap::from_bytes`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.from_dict(data: GlyphBitmap) -> Bitmap`

*static method* -- From the plain-data form produced by `to_dict`.

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.from_hex_rows(width: int, rows: Sequence[str], limits: BitmapLimits | None = ...) -> Bitmap`

*static method*

Parse strict BDF-style byte-padded hex rows into a Mono bitmap
(`Bitmap::<Mono>::from_hex_rows`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.from_raw(width: int, height: int, data: Buffer | Sequence[int], depth: Depth = ..., limits: BitmapLimits | None = ...) -> Bitmap`

*static method*

From canonical storage: top-down rows, Mono rows packed MSB-first and
padded to whole bytes, Gray8 one byte per pixel (`Bitmap::from_raw`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.from_rows(rows: Sequence[Buffer | Sequence[int]], depth: Depth = ..., limits: BitmapLimits | None = ...) -> Bitmap`

*static method* -- From a list of rows of pixel values, top row first (inverse of `to_rows`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.from_text(text: str, palette: TextPalette | None = ..., depth: Depth = ..., limits: BitmapLimits | None = ...) -> Bitmap`

*static method*

Parse text rows through `palette` (dict `{char: value}` or pairs); the
Mono default accepts `#`/`1` as ink and `.`/`0` as paper. Blank leading
and trailing lines are ignored (`Bitmap::from_text`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.get_pixel(x: int, y: int) -> int`

*method* -- Pixel value at `(x, y)` (`Bitmap::get_pixel`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.glow(diagonals: bool, ink: int, value: int) -> Bitmap`

*method* -- One-pixel glow around pixels equal to `ink` (`Bitmap::glow`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.has_ink() -> bool`

*method* -- Whether any pixel is nonzero (`Bitmap::has_ink`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.height: int`

*property* -- Height in pixels.

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.invert() -> None`

*method*

Binary inversion in place: zero becomes full ink, nonzero zero
(`Bitmap::invert`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.invert_with(ink: int) -> None`

*method* -- Binary inversion in place with ink value `ink` (`Bitmap::invert_with`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.italic(step: int, base: int = ...) -> Bitmap`

*method* -- Slant by `floor((row_from_bottom - base) / step)` (`Bitmap::italic`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.limits: BitmapLimits`

*property* -- The bitmap's resource limits as a dict (`Bitmap::limits`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.max_value: int`

*property* -- Largest pixel value: 1 for Mono, 255 for Gray8 (`PixelFormat::MAX`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.negate() -> None`

*method* -- Continuous-tone inversion `255 - v` in place (`Bitmap::<Gray8>::negate`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.overlay(source: BitmapLike) -> None`

*method* -- `paste(source, 0, 0)` (`Bitmap::overlay`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.packed: bool`

*property* -- Whether rows are bit-packed (`PixelFormat::PACKED`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.paste(source: BitmapLike, x: int = ..., y: int = ...) -> None`

*method* -- `composite(source, x, y, "over")` (`Bitmap::paste`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.replace(old: int, new: int) -> None`

*method* -- Replace every pixel equal to `old` with `new`, in place (`Bitmap::replace`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.replace_pattern(old: Buffer | Sequence[int], new: Buffer | Sequence[int]) -> Bitmap`

*method* -- Row-wise non-overlapping pattern replacement (`Bitmap::replace_pattern`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.rotate(degrees: int) -> Bitmap`

*method* -- Rotate clockwise by a multiple of 90 degrees (`Bitmap::rotate`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.set_limits(limits: BitmapLimits) -> None`

*method*

Replace the limits after checking the current size against them
(`Bitmap::set_limits`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.set_pixel(x: int, y: int, value: int) -> None`

*method* -- Set the pixel at `(x, y)`; the value must fit the depth (`Bitmap::set_pixel`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.shadow(dx: int, dy: int, value: int) -> Bitmap`

*method* -- Displaced silhouette behind the ink (`Bitmap::shadow`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.shift(dx: int, dy: int) -> Bitmap`

*method* -- Move pixels right/up inside the same size, filling with 0 (`Bitmap::shift`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.stride: int`

*property* -- Bytes per canonical row (`Bitmap::stride`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.to_bytes(layout: ByteLayout | None = ...) -> bytes`

*method*

Serialize in an explicit `ByteLayout` (default: MSB-first, byte rows,
top-down) (`Bitmap::to_bytes`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.to_dict() -> GlyphBitmap`

*method* -- Plain data: `{"mono" | "gray8": {"width", "height", "data": [...]}}`.

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.to_gray8() -> Bitmap`

*method* -- Gray8 copy with paper 0 and ink 255 (`Bitmap::<Mono>::to_gray8`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.to_gray8_palette(paper: int, ink: int) -> Bitmap`

*method*

Gray8 copy with explicit paper and ink values
(`Bitmap::<Mono>::to_gray8_palette`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.to_hex_rows() -> list[str]`

*method* -- Byte-padded uppercase hex rows (BDF storage) (`Bitmap::<Mono>::to_hex_rows`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.to_list() -> list[int]`

*method* -- Every pixel value in row-major order.

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.to_mono(threshold: int) -> Bitmap`

*method* -- Mono copy: ink where the value is `>= threshold` (`Bitmap::<Gray8>::to_mono`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.to_numeric_hex_rows() -> list[str]`

*method* -- Right-aligned lowercase hex rows (`Bitmap::<Mono>::to_numeric_hex_rows`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.to_palette_bytes(palette: Mapping[int, Buffer] | Iterable[tuple[int, Buffer]]) -> bytes`

*method*

One fixed-size byte string per pixel, from `palette` (dict
`{value: bytes}` or pairs) (`Bitmap::to_palette_bytes`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.to_row_values() -> list[int]`

*method*

Rows as integers, leftmost pixel most significant; width ≤ 64
(`Bitmap::<Mono>::to_row_values`).

#### `fontpixel.Bitmap.to_rows() -> list[list[int]]`

### `fontpixel.Properties(items: PropertiesLike | None = ...) -> Properties`

*class*

An ordered list of named properties (`fontpixel::model::Properties`).

Obtained from `FontSet.properties`, `Font.properties`, `Font.headers`,
`Font.localized_names` or `Glyph.properties`, it is a live view: `set`,
`push` and `remove` edit the owning model in place. `Properties(items)`
builds a standalone list; `copy()` detaches a view.

Values are given as Python values (`int` → Integer, or Unsigned above
the `i64` range; `str` → Text; `bytes` → Bytes; `list` → List;
`None` → Flag) or as the tagged plain-data form (`{"Decimal": "1.5"}`).
Values are returned in the tagged form, which keeps every variant.

#### `fontpixel.Properties.copy() -> Properties`

*method* -- A standalone copy.

#### `fontpixel.Properties.get(name: str) -> PropertyValue | None`

*method*

The value of the last property named exactly `name`, in tagged form,
or `None` (`Properties::get`).

#### `fontpixel.Properties.get_case_insensitive(name: str) -> PropertyValue | None`

*method*

Like `get`, comparing names ASCII-case-insensitively
(`Properties::get_case_insensitive`).

#### `fontpixel.Properties.is_empty() -> bool`

*method* -- Whether the list is empty (`Properties::is_empty`).

#### `fontpixel.Properties.push(name: str, value: PropertyValueLike, raw: Buffer | Sequence[int] | None = ...) -> None`

*method*

Append a property, keeping duplicates (`Properties::push` with
`Property::new`; `raw` is the optional source spelling).

#### `fontpixel.Properties.remove(name: str) -> int`

*method*

Remove every property whose name matches case-insensitively; returns
the number removed (`Properties::remove`).

#### `fontpixel.Properties.set(name: str, value: PropertyValueLike) -> None`

*method*

Replace the last property whose name matches case-insensitively, or
append a new one (`Properties::set`).

#### `fontpixel.Properties.to_list() -> list[Property]`

*method* -- A list of property dicts (`Properties::iter` / `into_vec`).

### `fontpixel.ReadContext(input: Input | Buffer, limits: ResourceLimits | None = ...) -> ReadContext`

*class*

Shared resource accounting for one input (`fontpixel::resources::ReadContext`).

Construction validates the primary input against `limits` and decodes a
gzip transport envelope. Each `resource*`/`list_resources_limited` call
counts against `max_resources` and the aggregate byte budget, exactly as
codecs see it. The context lives on a private worker thread (it borrows
its input); calls block until the worker answers, with the GIL released.

#### `fontpixel.ReadContext.bytes() -> bytes`

*method* -- Primary bytes after transport decoding (`ReadContext::bytes`).

#### `fontpixel.ReadContext.is_directory: bool`

*property* -- Whether the input is a directory entry point (`ReadContext::is_directory`).

#### `fontpixel.ReadContext.limits: ResourceLimits`

*property* -- The budgets in force (`ReadContext::limits`).

#### `fontpixel.ReadContext.list_resources_limited(directory: str | None, max_entries: int, max_bytes: int) -> list[str]`

*method*

List immediate files of `directory` with shared accounting
(`ReadContext::list_resources_limited`).

#### `fontpixel.ReadContext.name: str | None`

*property* -- The filename hint (`ReadContext::name`).

#### `fontpixel.ReadContext.resource(path: str) -> bytes`

*method* -- Resolve a sidecar under the remaining budget (`ReadContext::resource`).

#### `fontpixel.ReadContext.resource_limited(path: str, max_bytes: int) -> bytes`

*method* -- Resolve with an extra byte allowance (`ReadContext::resource_limited`).

#### `fontpixel.ReadContext.retained_input_bytes() -> int`

*method*

Bytes retained so far, including resolved resources
(`ReadContext::retained_input_bytes`).

### `fontpixel.Registry(builtin: bool = ...) -> Registry`

*class* -- The format registry (`fontpixel::Registry<FontSet>`).

#### `fontpixel.Registry.detect(data: ReadInput | None = ..., *, name: str | None = ..., resources: Resources | None = ..., limits: ResourceLimits | None = ..., directory: str | None = ...) -> Detected`

*method*

Detect the format of an input: content detectors first, the filename
hint only when no detector matches. Returns
`{"format": FormatInfo, "confidence": "certain"|"possible"|"extension"}`.
`directory` names a directory entry point (an error: directory inputs
need an explicit format).

#### `fontpixel.Registry.ensure_writable(format: str) -> None`

*method* -- Raise `NotImplementedFormatError` unless `format` has a writer.

#### `fontpixel.Registry.extension_candidates(name: str) -> list[FormatInfo]`

*method*

Formats whose extension is the longest matching suffix of `name`
(`FormatInfo` dicts; ties are all returned).

#### `fontpixel.Registry.format_from_name(name: str) -> FormatInfo`

*method*

The unique `FormatInfo` for a filename; raises `UnrecognizedFormatError`
or `AmbiguousFormatError` (with `candidates`).

#### `fontpixel.Registry.formats() -> list[FormatStatus]`

*method*

Every catalogue format with its capabilities, as `FormatStatus` dicts
(`{"format": {"id", "name", "extensions", "feature_enabled"}, "detect",
"read", "write"}`).

#### `fontpixel.Registry.read(data: ReadInput | None = ..., format: str | None = ..., *, name: str | None = ..., resources: Resources | None = ..., limits: ResourceLimits | None = ..., directory: str | None = ...) -> Loaded`

*method*

Decode an input (`Registry::read`). `format` bypasses detection;
`limits` is a `ResourceLimits` dict; `resources` supplies sidecars;
`directory="name"` reads a native directory entry point whose files come
from `resources` (an explicit format is then required).

#### `fontpixel.Registry.register(format: str | NewFormat, *, detector: Callable[[ReadContext], Confidence] | None = ..., reader: Callable[[ReadContext, FormatsReadOptions], tuple[FontSet, Report]] | None = ..., writer: PythonWriter | None = ...) -> None`

*method*

Register a format implemented in Python (`Registry::register` with a
`Registration`). `format` is a catalogue ID or
`{"id", "name", "extensions"}` for a new ID (lowercase ASCII letters,
digits and hyphens). Without hooks this is an honest planned entry
(`Registration::planned`). A live entry cannot be replaced: use
`Registry(builtin=False)` to register a catalogue ID.

#### `fontpixel.Registry.write(fonts: FontSet | Font, format: str, *, report: Report | None = ..., primary_name: str | None = ..., strict: bool = ..., transport_limits: TransportLimits | None = ...) -> Written`

*method*

Encode a `FontSet` (or one `Font`) as `format` (`Registry::write`, or
`write_with_report` when `report` carries earlier read diagnostics).
`primary_name` defaults to `font.<first extension>`; a `.gz` suffix
selects the gzip envelope. `strict=True` raises `StrictLossError` on
any read or write loss. `transport_limits` is a `TransportLimits` dict.

#### `fontpixel.Registry.write_owned(fonts: FontSet | Font, format: str, report: Report | None = ..., *, primary_name: str | None = ..., strict: bool = ..., transport_limits: TransportLimits | None = ...) -> Written`

*method*

`Registry::write_owned`: hand the model over so it can be released
before later encoder stages. A `FontSet` argument is *moved*: the
handle is left empty (zero strikes) afterwards. Output and report equal
`write_with_report`; `transport_limits` include the model.

#### `fontpixel.Registry.write_reserved_with_report(fonts: FontSet | Font, format: str, report: Report | None = ..., *, primary_name: str | None = ..., strict: bool = ..., transport_limits: TransportLimits | None = ...) -> Written`

*method*

`Registry::write_reserved_with_report`: as `write_with_report` while the
caller keeps the model's retained usage reserved outside
`transport_limits`. Output and report are identical.

#### `fontpixel.Registry.write_with_report(fonts: FontSet | Font, format: str, report: Report, *, primary_name: str | None = ..., strict: bool = ..., transport_limits: TransportLimits | None = ...) -> Written`

*method*

`Registry::write_with_report`: combine `report` (earlier read
diagnostics, a dict) with the write diagnostics before strict checks.

*function*

Apply `projection` (a `BitmapProjection` or a dict of its constructor
arguments) to every strike as one transaction; on error the set is
unchanged (`projection::apply_bitmap_projection`). Returns the
`ProjectionOutcome` dict (`report`, `scalable_advance_changes`,
`metadata_changes`) plus `retained_bytes`
(`ProjectionOutcome::retained_bytes`). `max_working_bytes` defaults to
unbounded.

dict (`family`, `style`, `full_name`, `postscript_name`, `version`,
`copyright`, `license`, `license_url`, `foundry`); an empty dict changes
nothing. Returns the report.

*function*

Encode a `FontSet` (or one `Font`) with the built-in registry
(`fontpixel::write`, or `write_with_report` when `report` is given).

`options` is the format's typed write-options dict. `primary_name`
defaults to `font.<first extension>`; a `.gz` suffix selects the gzip

## fontpixel.compat

Compatibility layers over the native fontpixel core.

## fontpixel.compat.bdfparser

bdfparser-compatible API (bdfparser 3.0 / SPEC-v3) on the fontpixel Rust core.

`Font`, `Glyph`, `Bitmap`, the module functions (`encoding`, `outline`, `pcf`,
`ttf`, `cli`), `BDFParserWarning` and `BDFParseError` behave as in bdfparser.
Font data stays in Rust: `Font`/`Glyph` hold handles and `Bitmap` wraps a
native raster; pixels are converted to row strings only when requested.

### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.BDFParseError(ValueError)`

*exception*

Raised on fatal BDF parse errors (unexpected end of file inside the headers,
malformed numbers in required fields, glyph without `BBX`, ...).

`lineno` is the 1-based line number where the problem was detected (or `None`).

### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.BDFParserWarning(UserWarning)`

*exception*

Category of every warning emitted by the compatibility API (non-fatal
problems in a font, missing glyphs, unknown charsets, ...).

Filter them with the standard `warnings` machinery, e.g.
`warnings.simplefilter('ignore', BDFParserWarning)`.

### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.Bitmap(bin_bitmap_list: Iterable[str]) -> Bitmap`

*class*

A bitmap of `'0'`/`'1'`/`'2'` rows (row 0 at the top), backed by a native
raster. Equality compares pixels; instances are unhashable (mutable).

#### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.Bitmap.bbox() -> tuple[int, int, int, int]`

*method* -- Ink bounding box `(w, h, xoff, yoff)`, bottom-left origin (`Bitmap::bbox`).

#### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.Bitmap.bindata: list[str]`

*property* -- The rows as a new list of strings (`Bitmap::bindata`); assign to replace.

#### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.Bitmap.blank(w: int, h: int) -> Self`

*class method* -- An all-zero `w`×`h` bitmap (`Bitmap::blank`).

#### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.Bitmap.bold(n: int = ...) -> Bitmap`

*method* -- Embolden by `n` pixels (`Bitmap::bold`).

#### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.Bitmap.bytepad(bits: int = ...) -> Bitmap`

*method* -- Pad the width to a multiple of `bits` (`Bitmap::bytepad`).

#### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.Bitmap.clone() -> Self`

*method* -- Independent copy.

## fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.bitmap

`Bitmap` of the bdfparser-compatible API.

`Bitmap` is the native class `fontpixel._native._bdfparser.Bitmap`: the pixels
live in a Rust raster of labels 0, 1 and 2; `bindata` builds the row strings on
request. Rows must be rectangular and made of `'0'`, `'1'` and `'2'`.

### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.bitmap.Bitmap`

*class* -- Same class as `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.Bitmap`.

### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.bitmap.fmtnum(n: 'float') -> 'str'`

*function*

Shortest text of a number as written in SVG output: integral values without
a fraction (`3.0` -> `'3'`, `-0.0` -> `'0'`), others as Python `repr`.

## fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.cli

Command line interface of the bdfparser-compatible API: `convert | info | preview`.

Same arguments, output and exit codes as `bdfparser`'s console script; every
font operation goes through the compatibility `Font` (Rust core).
Run as `python -m fontpixel.compat.bdfparser`.

### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.cli.main(argv: 'Sequence[str] | None' = None) -> 'int'`

*function* -- Entry point of the `bdfparser`-compatible command line. Returns the exit status.

## fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.encoding

Charset support of the bdfparser-compatible API (SPEC-v3 §4, §11.1).

Every function delegates to the native charset API (`fontpixel.CharsetCodec`,
`fontpixel.canonical_charset`, ... over `fontpixel::charset`, generated from
CPython's codecs): canonical keys, `CHARSET_REGISTRY` /
`CHARSET_ENCODING` folding, strict one-character conversions and GL forms.

### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.encoding.CharsetCodec(name: 'str', codec: 'str | None' = None, gl: 'bool' = False, known: 'bool' = True) -> None`

*class*

Converter between glyph codepoints and characters for one charset: `name`
(canonical key), `codec` (CPython codec name, `None` for Unicode), `gl`
(2-byte codes stored in GL form), `known` (unknown charsets map as Unicode).

#### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.encoding.CharsetCodec.char2cp(self, char: 'str') -> 'int | None'`

*method* -- Codepoint of a single character, `None` if not representable.

#### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.encoding.CharsetCodec.codec: NoneType`

*constant*

#### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.encoding.CharsetCodec.cp2char(self, cp: 'int') -> 'str | None'`

*method* -- Character of a codepoint, `None` if not representable.

#### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.encoding.CharsetCodec.gl: bool`

*constant*

#### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.encoding.CharsetCodec.kind`

*property* -- `'unicode'`, `'sbcs'`, `'dbcs'` or `'gb18030'`.

#### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.encoding.CharsetCodec.known: bool`

*constant*

### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.encoding.UNICODE_PREFIXES: tuple`

*constant*

### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.encoding.canonical_charset(name: 'str') -> 'str'`

*function* -- Canonical key of any charset spelling (`'GB2312'`, `'Shift-JIS'`, ...).

### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.encoding.char2cp(char: 'str', charset: 'str' = 'iso10646', gl: 'bool | None' = None) -> 'int | None'`

*function* -- Character -> codepoint in a charset (any spelling); `None` if not representable.

### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.encoding.charset_codec(key: 'str', gl: 'bool | None' = None) -> 'CharsetCodec'`

*function*

`CharsetCodec` for a canonical key. `gl=None`: GL form only for charsets that
are always GL (`iso2022cn`); GL is ignored for charsets that are not 94x94.

### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.encoding.charset_map(key: 'str') -> 'dict[int, str]'`

*function*

Every valid 1- and 2-byte code of a non-Unicode charset (non-GL form) ->
its character, as `charset_codec(key, gl=False).cp2char` converts it.

### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.encoding.charset_props(key: 'str') -> 'tuple[str, str]'`

*function* -- `(CHARSET_REGISTRY, CHARSET_ENCODING)` written by `Font.charsetconvert`.

### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.encoding.charset_table() -> 'dict[str, dict[str, Any]]'`

*function*

The canonical charset table `{key: info}`; `info` has `codec`, `kind`
(`'unicode'`, `'sbcs'`, `'dbcs'`, `'gb18030'`), `gl`, `forcegl`, `props` and
`aliases`.

### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.encoding.codec_name(key: 'str') -> 'str | None'`

*function* -- CPython codec name of a known non-Unicode key (`None` otherwise).

### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.encoding.cp2char(cp: 'int', charset: 'str' = 'iso10646', gl: 'bool | None' = None) -> 'str | None'`

*function* -- Codepoint in a charset -> character; `None` if not representable.

### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.encoding.gb18030_ranges() -> 'list[tuple[int, int, int]]'`

*function*

The 4-byte GB18030 codes as runs `(index, codepoint, length)`, where for a
code `b0 b1 b2 b3`:
`index = (((b0 - 0x81) * 10 + (b1 - 0x30)) * 126 + (b2 - 0x81)) * 10 + (b3 - 0x30)`.

### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.encoding.is_unicode_charset(key: 'str') -> 'bool'`

*function* -- Whether a canonical key denotes Unicode identity (UTF prefixes included).

### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.encoding.sanitize_charset(registry: 'object' = None, encoding: 'object' = None) -> 'str'`

*function*

Canonical charset key from `CHARSET_REGISTRY` / `CHARSET_ENCODING` values
(`'iso10646'` when both are absent).

## fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.errors

Warning and exception classes of the bdfparser-compatible API.

bdfparser raises built-in exceptions (`ValueError`, `KeyError`, `OSError`, ...)
plus `BDFParseError` / `PCFError`. Errors coming from the Rust core are
translated by `_translate`: the raised class derives from both the bdfparser
class and the matching `fontpixel` exception (so `except ValueError` and
`except fontpixel.InvalidInputError` both work) and keeps the structured
attributes (`kind`, `resource`, `limit`, `line`, `report`, ...).

### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.errors.BDFParseError`

*class* -- Same class as `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.BDFParseError`.

### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.errors.BDFParserWarning`

*class* -- Same class as `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.BDFParserWarning`.

## fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.font

`Font` of the bdfparser-compatible API (handle over the Rust compat font).

The font data stays in the Rust model (`fontpixel::compat::bdfparser::Font`).
`headers`, `props`, `glyphs` and `unencoded` are live views: reading them
projects the current model, writing through them edits it in place (glyph
handles stay attached). Values read from them are fresh copies (editing a
returned list does not change the font, except for the 17-slot meta lists of
`font.glyphs[cp]` and `font.unencoded[i]['meta']`, whose item assignment is
written back). Warnings collected by the Rust model are re-emitted as
`BDFParserWarning`s through the `warnings` module after each call.

### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.font.Font`

*class* -- Same class as `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.Font`.

## fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.glyph

`Glyph` of the bdfparser-compatible API (handle over the Rust compat glyph).

A glyph obtained from a font (`glyphbycp`, `glyph`, `iterglyphs`, `newglyph`,
or passed to `addglyph`) is *attached*: every editing method writes the updated
meta back into the font's native model immediately. A glyph constructed
directly, or a `clone()`, is detached.

### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.glyph.Glyph`

*class* -- Same class as `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.Glyph`.

### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.glyph.META_TITLES: tuple[str, ...]`

*constant*

### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.glyph.defaultglyphname(cp: int, charset_is_unicode: bool = ...) -> str`

*function* -- `defaultglyphname(cp, charset_is_unicode=True)`: `uniXXXX`, `uXXXXX` or `charN`.

## fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.outline

Bitmap outlines of the bdfparser-compatible API (SPEC-v3 §7.1, §7.2, §7.4).

`bitmap_contours` and `rasterize` run the Rust SPEC outline code. A contour is
a list of `(x, y, on_curve)` points in font units, y up.

### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.outline.Contour(iterable=(), /)`

*class*

Built-in mutable sequence.

If no argument is given, the constructor creates a new empty list.
The argument must be an iterable if specified.

### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.outline.Point(iterable=(), /)`

*class*

Built-in immutable sequence.

If no argument is given, the constructor returns an empty tuple.
If iterable is specified the tuple is initialized from iterable's items.

If the argument is a tuple, the return value is the same object.

### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.outline.bitmap_contours(bindata: 'Sequence[str]', shape: 'str' = 'square', dotsize: 'float' = 1.0, ppu: 'int' = 1, xoff: 'int' = 0, yoff: 'int' = 0) -> 'list[Contour]'`

*function*

Convert bitmap rows (top row first, any non-`'0'` pixel is ink) to
TrueType-style contours: `shape` `'square'` (merged outline when
`dotsize == 1`) or `'circle'`; `ppu` font units per pixel; `(xoff, yoff)`
the bottom-left pixel position.

### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.outline.rasterize(contours: 'Iterable[Sequence[tuple[float, float, bool]]]', ppu: 'float', xmin_px: 'int', ymin_px: 'int', w_px: 'int', h_px: 'int') -> 'list[str]'`

*function*

Rasterize contours (nonzero winding, pixel centres, 16 chords per quadratic
curve) into `h_px` rows of `w_px` pixels whose bottom-left pixel is at
`(xmin_px, ymin_px)`.

## fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.pcf

PCF input/output of the bdfparser-compatible API (SPEC-v3 §6).

Reading and writing use the native, bounded PCF codec. With default options the
output is byte-identical to `bdftopcf` run on the same BDF.

### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.pcf.PCFError(BDFParseError)`

*exception*

Raised for malformed PCF data or fonts that cannot be written as PCF.
Subclass of `BDFParseError` (itself a `ValueError`).

### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.pcf.read_pcf(data: 'bytes | bytearray | memoryview') -> 'Font'`

*function* -- Parse PCF (optionally gzip-compressed) bytes into a `Font`; `PCFError` on malformed input.

### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.pcf.write_pcf(font: 'Font', *, byteorder: 'str' = 'msb', bitorder: 'str' = 'msb', glyphpad: 'int' = 4, scanunit: 'int' = 1) -> 'bytes'`

*function*

Convert a font to PCF bytes. `byteorder`/`bitorder`: `'msb'` or `'lsb'`
(bdftopcf -M/-L, -m/-l); `glyphpad`: 1, 2, 4 or 8 (-p); `scanunit`: 1, 2 or
4 (-u).

## fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.ttf

Pixel TrueType output/input of the bdfparser-compatible API (SPEC-v3 §8, §8.1).

Both directions run the Rust compatibility writer/reader; output is
deterministic and byte-identical to bdfparser's.

### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.ttf.read_ttf(data: 'bytes | bytearray | memoryview', pixelsize: 'int | None' = None) -> 'Font'`

*function*

Read a TrueType (`glyf`) font. Fonts written by `write_ttf` with
`metadata=True` are restored losslessly; others are rasterized at
`pixelsize` pixels per em (required then).

### `fontpixel.compat.bdfparser.ttf.write_ttf(font: 'Font', *, shape: 'str' = 'square', dotsize: 'float' = 1.0, ppu: 'int' = 64, metadata: 'bool' = True, timestamp: 'int' = 0) -> 'bytes'`

*function*

Convert a font to a TrueType font with square or round pixel dots.

:param shape: `'square'` or `'circle'` dots.
:param dotsize: dot size relative to a pixel, `(0, 1.5]`.
:param ppu: font units per pixel (even integer >= 2).
:param metadata: embed the private `BDFP` table (lossless `read_ttf` round trip).
:param timestamp: Unix seconds for `head.created` / `head.modified`.

## fontpixel.ops

Every fontpixel command-line operation as an in-process call.

Each operation takes a request dict in the flat ``fontpixel_ops`` shape (keys
are the command-line argument ids in snake_case: ``inputs``, ``output``, ``to``,
``max_total_bytes``, ``otb_upm``, ...) and/or the same keys as keyword
arguments. Unknown keys, invalid choices, out-of-range numbers and violated
command-line rules (``each`` without ``to``, ``text`` together with ``all``,
...) raise :class:`fontpixel.InvalidInputError` with ``exit_code`` 2 and the
command-line parser's message.

Storage is chosen per call with ``files``:

* ``files=None`` (default) -- filesystem mode: request paths are real paths
  (``str`` or ``os.PathLike``), sidecars are discovered beside their primary
  file, sources are protected from being overwritten and every multi-output
  group is written transactionally, exactly as ``fontpixel`` does.
* ``files={"name.bdf": b"...", ...}`` or a :class:`fontpixel.ResourceSet` --
  memory mode: paths are keys into the named buffers (``bytes``, ``bytearray``
  or ``memoryview``); sidecars resolve beside their primary key and a key
  prefix acts as a directory. Nothing is read from or written to disk;
  ``result.outputs`` maps each prepared asset's key to its bytes and
  ``result.bundles`` each destination to its :class:`fontpixel.OutputBundle`.
* ``files=<resolver>`` -- memory mode over an object with ``entry(path)``
  (``None``, a file length or ``"directory"``), ``read(path) -> bytes`` and
  ``list(directory) -> list[str]``; an exception raised by a callback is
  re-raised from the operation.

Results (:class:`OperationResult`, :class:`BatchResult`) reproduce the command
line's standard output: ``result.json()`` is the ``--report json``/``--json``
document and ``result.text()`` the text output, byte for byte. Failures raise
the ``fontpixel`` exception classes with ``exit_code`` (the command-line exit
status), ``kind`` and, for strict-loss and reported errors, the full
``report``. The GIL is released while an operation runs, so calls from several
threads proceed in parallel.

:func:`merge`, :func:`convert` and :func:`vectorize` accept
``progress=callback``: the callback receives a :class:`fontpixel.types.Progress`
dict (``step`` ``"read"``, ``"merge"`` or ``"encode"``, ``done``, ``total``,
``item``, ``glyphs``, ``bytes``) after each step, on the calling thread with
the GIL held, before anything is written. Returning ``False`` (exactly) cancels
the operation with :class:`fontpixel.CancelledError` (``exit_code`` 1);
raising cancels it and re-raises that exception. Nothing is written or
returned after a cancellation, and results never depend on the callback.

Example::

    from fontpixel import ops
    result = ops.convert(inputs=["font.bdf"], output="font.pcf",
                         files={"font.bdf": open("font.bdf", "rb").read()})
    pcf = result.outputs["font.pcf"]

### `fontpixel.ops.BatchResult()`

*class* -- The result of a batch: the complete JSON document plus typed summaries.

#### `fontpixel.ops.BatchResult.bundles: dict[str, OutputBundle]`

*property*

Committed outputs as `{destination key: fontpixel.OutputBundle}`
(memory mode only).

#### `fontpixel.ops.BatchResult.document: dict[str, Any]`

*property* -- The parsed batch document.

#### `fontpixel.ops.BatchResult.exit_code: int`

*property* -- Aggregate exit code (precedence 2 > 1 > 3 > 0), as `fontpixel batch`.

#### `fontpixel.ops.BatchResult.jobs: int`

*property* -- Requested worker ceiling, capped by the task count.

#### `fontpixel.ops.BatchResult.json() -> str`

*method* -- The complete batch JSON document exactly as `fontpixel batch` prints it.

#### `fontpixel.ops.BatchResult.outputs: dict[str, bytes]`

*property* -- Committed outputs as `{storage key: bytes}` (memory mode only).

#### `fontpixel.ops.BatchResult.tasks: list[BatchTaskOutcome]`

*property*

Per-task outcomes in request order (dicts with `index`, `id`, `kind`,
`success`, `exit_code`, `committed`, `diagnostics_truncated`, `error`).

#### `fontpixel.ops.BatchResult.workers: int`

*property* -- Worker threads actually used.

### `fontpixel.ops.OperationResult()`

*class*

The result of one operation.

`json()` and `text()` reproduce the command line's standard output for the
JSON and text report styles; `document` is the parsed JSON document,
`summary` the typed response fields, `report` the operation's diagnostics
(or `None` when it has several, see `summary`), and `outputs` maps every
prepared asset's storage key to its bytes (memory mode only).

#### `fontpixel.ops.OperationResult.bundles: dict[str, OutputBundle]`

*property*

Every prepared output as `{destination key: fontpixel.OutputBundle}`
(memory mode; the bundle holds the primary asset and its sidecars or
directory members, with paths relative to the destination's parent).

#### `fontpixel.ops.OperationResult.destinations: list[str]`

*property* -- The requested entry-point destination of each prepared output.

#### `fontpixel.ops.OperationResult.document: dict[str, Any]`

*property* -- The parsed JSON document (a dict), equal to `json.loads(self.json())`.

#### `fontpixel.ops.OperationResult.exit_code: int`

*property*

Command-line exit status of a completed operation: 0, or 1 for a diff
that found differences.

#### `fontpixel.ops.OperationResult.font_json(index: int, pretty: bool = ...) -> str`

*method* -- The JSON metadata of one decoded font (`info` only).

#### `fontpixel.ops.OperationResult.fonts: FontSet | None`

*property* -- Decoded fonts of an `info` call as a `fontpixel.FontSet`, else `None`.

#### `fontpixel.ops.OperationResult.format_status(id: str) -> FormatStatus | None`

*method* -- The status dict of one format identifier (`formats` only), or `None`.

#### `fontpixel.ops.OperationResult.json(pretty: bool = ...) -> str`

*method*

The command-line JSON document (`--report json` / `--json` stdout):
pretty for standalone commands, compact as in batch task results.

#### `fontpixel.ops.OperationResult.operation: str`

*property* -- Operation name (`"convert"`, `"merge"`, …).

#### `fontpixel.ops.OperationResult.outputs: dict[str, bytes]`

*property*

Every prepared asset as `{storage key: bytes}` (memory mode; empty
after filesystem mode, where the outputs were already committed).

#### `fontpixel.ops.OperationResult.report: Report | None`

*property*

The operation's diagnostics report, or `None` for operations with one
report per output or input (convert, merge, diff, formats).

#### `fontpixel.ops.OperationResult.summary: dict[str, Any]`

*property* -- Typed response fields as plain data (per operation; see the module docs).

#### `fontpixel.ops.OperationResult.text() -> str`

*method* -- The command line's text-mode standard output.

### `fontpixel.ops.batch(request: BatchRequest | None = ..., /, *, files: Files | None = ..., **options: Any) -> BatchResult`

*function*

Run typed tasks as one batch (`fontpixel batch` with typed tasks).

Request keys: `tasks` (list of request dicts, each with `id` and a `kind`
of `convert`, `vectorize`, `variants`, `subset`, `merge`, `charset`,
`validate` or `diff`), `jobs`, `max_working_bytes`, `max_pending_bytes`,
`max_report_bytes`, `max_task_report_bytes` and `protected_paths`. A task
whose request is invalid fails alone with exit code 2. Every successful
writer joins one output transaction (filesystem) or the returned outputs
(memory). A whole-batch failure raises with a `document` attribute.

### `fontpixel.ops.batch_file(path: StrPath, /, *, jobs: int | None = ...) -> BatchResult`

*function*

Run a TOML job file from the filesystem exactly as `fontpixel batch FILE
[--jobs N]` (the job file is protected from every output; `jobs` is
1..=64).

### `fontpixel.ops.batch_toml(text: str, /, *, base: StrPath | None = ..., jobs: int | None = ..., files: Files | None = ...) -> BatchResult`

*function*

Run a version-1 TOML job text (the `fontpixel batch` file format).
Relative paths resolve against `base`; `jobs` overrides the file's
worker ceiling.

### `fontpixel.ops.capabilities() -> Capabilities`

*function*

Platform capabilities of this build: `filesystem`, `threads` and
`toml_batch` (bools).

### `fontpixel.ops.charset(request: CharsetRequest | None = ..., /, *, files: Files | None = ..., **options: Any) -> OperationResult`

*function*

Remap glyph codes into another charset and write the result
(`fontpixel charset`).

### `fontpixel.ops.convert(request: ConvertRequest | None = ..., /, *, files: Files | None = ..., progress: Callable[[Progress], object] | None = ..., **options: Any) -> OperationResult`

*function*

Convert inputs into one output, or each input into its own output
(`fontpixel convert`). Request keys: `inputs`, `output`, `from`, `to`,
`each`, `strict`, `font_index`, `report` and every reader/writer option.

`progress`, if given, is called with a dict
`{"step", "done", "total", "item", "glyphs", "bytes"}` after each input
is read (`step` `"read"`) and each output is encoded (`"encode"`).
Returning `False` cancels with `CancelledError`; raising cancels and
re-raises; nothing is written either way. Results do not depend on it.

### `fontpixel.ops.diff(request: DiffRequest | None = ..., /, *, files: Files | None = ..., **options: Any) -> OperationResult`

*function*

Compare two inputs (`fontpixel diff`). Differences are reported in the
result (`summary["equal"]`, `exit_code` 1), not raised.

### `fontpixel.ops.formats(request: FormatsRequest | None = ..., /, **options: Any) -> OperationResult`

*function*

List every catalogue format with the reader/writer compiled into this
build (`fontpixel formats`).

### `fontpixel.ops.info(request: InfoRequest | None = ..., /, *, files: Files | None = ..., **options: Any) -> OperationResult`

*function*

Decode one input and describe its fonts (`fontpixel info`); the result's
`fonts` is the decoded `fontpixel.FontSet`.

### `fontpixel.ops.inspect_request(operation: str, request: Mapping[str, Any] | None = ..., /, **options: Any) -> InspectedRequest`

*function*

Validate a request for `operation` and describe it: the normalized
`request` (every default filled in), `report_style`,
`source_identity_total_bytes` and, for batch task kinds, `declared_inputs`
and `weight`. Raises `InvalidInputError` (exit code 2) exactly when the
operation would reject the request before running.

### `fontpixel.ops.memory_key(path: StrPath) -> str`

*function* -- The memory-storage key of a path: `.` removed, `..` folded, `/` separators.

### `fontpixel.ops.merge(request: MergeRequest | None = ..., /, *, files: Files | None = ..., progress: Callable[[Progress], object] | None = ..., **options: Any) -> OperationResult`

*function*

Merge selected glyphs from ordered parts and write every output as one
group (`fontpixel merge`). Request keys: `parts` (list of
`{input, take, dy, from, font_index}`), `outputs` (list of
`{destination, format}`), `family` and the merge/writer options.

`progress`, if given, is called with a dict
`{"step", "done", "total", "item", "glyphs", "bytes"}` after each part
is read (`"read"`), after the merge (`"merge"`) and after each output
is encoded (`"encode"`), before anything is written. Returning `False`
cancels with `CancelledError`; raising cancels and re-raises; nothing
is written either way. Results do not depend on it.

### `fontpixel.ops.output_format_for(destination: StrPath) -> str`

*function*

The output format `convert` infers for a destination path (OpenType
container extensions first, then the registry's filename hints); an
ambiguous or unknown extension raises like `convert` without `to`.

### `fontpixel.ops.parse_args(argv: Sequence[str]) -> ParsedArgs`

*function*

Parse a `fontpixel` command line (without the program name) with the
command-line definition and return `{"command", "request", "report_style",
"source_identity_total_bytes"}`; `request` can be passed to the matching
operation. A rejected command line raises `InvalidInputError` with the
parser's message and `exit_code` (0 for `--help`/`--version`).

### `fontpixel.ops.parse_batch_toml(text: str, /, *, base: StrPath | None = ...) -> ParsedBatch`

*function*

Parse a TOML job text without running it: the tasks as dicts with `id`,
`kind`, `declared_inputs` and either `request` (the normalized request)
and `weight`, or `error` for a task that failed preparation.

### `fontpixel.ops.preview(request: PreviewRequest | None = ..., /, *, files: Files | None = ..., **options: Any) -> OperationResult`

*function*

Lay out text (or every mapping) as character art (`fontpixel preview`):
`text()` is the art, `json()` the diagnostics document.

### `fontpixel.ops.render(request: RenderRequest | None = ..., /, *, files: Files | None = ..., **options: Any) -> OperationResult`

*function*

Lay out text (or every mapping with `all=True`) into a PNG or SVG image
(`fontpixel render`).

### `fontpixel.ops.subset(request: SubsetRequest | None = ..., /, *, files: Files | None = ..., **options: Any) -> OperationResult`

*function* -- Subset an sfnt, WOFF or WOFF2 font (`fontpixel subset`).

### `fontpixel.ops.validate(request: ValidateRequest | None = ..., /, *, files: Files | None = ..., **options: Any) -> OperationResult`

*function* -- Validate one input (`fontpixel validate`).

### `fontpixel.ops.variants(request: VariantsRequest | None = ..., /, *, files: Files | None = ..., **options: Any) -> OperationResult`

*function*

Build a locl-enabled OpenType font from regional and script faces
(`fontpixel variants`).

### `fontpixel.ops.vectorize(request: 'ConvertRequest | None' = None, /, *, files: 'Files | None' = None, progress: 'Callable[[Progress], object] | None' = None, **options: 'Any') -> 'OperationResult'`

*function*

Vectorize (``fontpixel vectorize``): the same operation as :func:`convert`.

The command-line ``vectorize`` is an alias of ``convert``; the result is
identical, including its JSON and text documents. ``progress`` behaves as
in :func:`convert`.

## fontpixel.sfnt

Bounded sfnt container, OpenType tables, collections, CFF and subsetting.

### `fontpixel.sfnt.Sfnt(data: Buffer | Sequence[int], limits: SfntLimits | None = ...) -> Sfnt`

*class*

A parsed standalone sfnt (`fontpixel::sfnt::Sfnt`).

The handle owns the input bytes and the `Limits` it was validated with;
every method re-parses the directory from those bytes.

#### `fontpixel.sfnt.Sfnt.data: bytes`

*property* -- The font bytes this handle owns.

#### `fontpixel.sfnt.Sfnt.flavor: Flavor`

*property* -- Outline flavor: `"true_type"`, `"cff"` or `"apple_true_type"`.

#### `fontpixel.sfnt.Sfnt.limits: SfntLimits`

*property* -- The limits dict used for parsing.

#### `fontpixel.sfnt.Sfnt.parse(data: Buffer | Sequence[int], limits: SfntLimits | None = ...) -> Sfnt`

*static method*

Parse a standalone sfnt directory, checking table bounds and limits.

`limits` is a `fontpixel.sfnt` Limits dict (see `defaults()`); checksums
are checked separately by `validate_checksums()`.

#### `fontpixel.sfnt.Sfnt.table(tag: Tag) -> bytes | None`

*method* -- The bytes of table `tag` (`str` such as `"OS/2"` or 4 `bytes`), or `None`.

#### `fontpixel.sfnt.Sfnt.tables() -> list[TableRecord]`

*method* -- Directory records in tag order: dicts `{tag, checksum, offset, data}`.

#### `fontpixel.sfnt.Sfnt.validate_checksums() -> None`

*method* -- Check every table checksum and the head checksum adjustment.

### `fontpixel.sfnt.SfntBuilder(flavor: Flavor) -> SfntBuilder`

*class* -- Assembles a standalone sfnt (`fontpixel::sfnt::SfntBuilder`).

#### `fontpixel.sfnt.SfntBuilder.build(limits: SfntLimits | None = ...) -> bytes`

*method* -- Build the font with sorted tables, checksums and head adjustment.

#### `fontpixel.sfnt.SfntBuilder.insert(tag: Tag, table: Buffer | Sequence[int]) -> None`

*method* -- Add table `tag`; duplicate or malformed tags raise `InvalidInputError`.

### `fontpixel.sfnt.checksum(data: Buffer | Sequence[int]) -> int`

*function* -- `fontpixel::sfnt::checksum`: wrapping big-endian 32-bit word sum.

### `fontpixel.sfnt.defaults() -> SfntDefaults`

*function*

Default limit and option dicts of `fontpixel.sfnt` and its submodules,
keyed by Rust type path relative to `fontpixel::sfnt`.

### `fontpixel.sfnt.flavor_version(flavor: Flavor) -> int`

*function* -- `Flavor::version`: the four-byte sfnt version of a flavor string.

## fontpixel.variants

Regional bitmap alternatives, deduplication and locl-enabled OpenType output.

### `fontpixel.variants.PreparedVariants()`

*class*

An immutable plan ready for repeated exports
(`fontpixel::variants::PreparedVariants`). Safe to share between threads.

#### `fontpixel.variants.PreparedVariants.encode(options: ExportOptions | None = ...) -> EncodedFont`

*method*

`PreparedVariants::encode`: export without replanning; `options.limits`
must equal the limits given to `prepare`.

#### `fontpixel.variants.PreparedVariants.encode_allowance() -> int`

*method*

`PreparedVariants::encode_allowance`: bytes one `encode` may admit
besides the plan.

#### `fontpixel.variants.PreparedVariants.plan() -> Plan`

*method* -- `PreparedVariants::plan`: the Plan dict.

#### `fontpixel.variants.PreparedVariants.retained_bytes() -> int`

*method* -- `PreparedVariants::retained_bytes`: admitted bytes of the shared plan.

### `fontpixel.variants.Variants(base: FontLike) -> Variants`

*class*

One default face plus ordered language and script alternatives
(`fontpixel::variants::Variants`).

Holds the model behind a lock; calls copy a reference to the current
model and release the lock (and the GIL) while working.

#### `fontpixel.variants.Variants.add_language(language: str, font: FontLike) -> None`

*method*

`Variants::add_language`: add a BCP-47/OpenType language with the
default CJK script scope (DFLT, hani, kana, hang, bopo).

#### `fontpixel.variants.Variants.add_language_variant(language: Tag, scripts: Iterable[Tag], font: FontLike) -> None`

*method*

Append a language alternative with explicit OpenType `language` tag and
`scripts` tags (the `languages` field).

#### `fontpixel.variants.Variants.add_script(scripts: Iterable[Tag], font: FontLike) -> None`

*method* -- Append a script alternative for `scripts` tags (the `scripts` field).

#### `fontpixel.variants.Variants.base: Font`

*property* -- A copy of the default face as a `Font` handle.

#### `fontpixel.variants.Variants.consumed: bool`

*property* -- Whether `encode_owned()`/`into_prepared()` consumed this handle.

#### `fontpixel.variants.Variants.encode(options: ExportOptions | None = ...) -> EncodedFont`

*method* -- `variants::encode`: plan and export (`{bytes, report}`).

#### `fontpixel.variants.Variants.encode_owned(options: ExportOptions | None = ...) -> EncodedFont`

*method*

`Variants::encode_owned`: plan and export, consuming this handle's
model and dropping faces as soon as they are planned.

#### `fontpixel.variants.Variants.from_dict(value: VariantsDict) -> Variants`

*static method* -- Build from a serde Variants dict `{base, languages, scripts}`.

#### `fontpixel.variants.Variants.into_prepared(limits: LayoutLimits | None = ...) -> PreparedVariants`

*method* -- `Variants::into_prepared`: as `prepare`, consuming this handle's model.

#### `fontpixel.variants.Variants.languages: list[LanguageVariantItem]`

*property*

Language alternatives as `[{language, scripts, font}]` (OpenType tag
strings, `Font` handle copies), in application order.

#### `fontpixel.variants.Variants.plan(limits: LayoutLimits | None = ...) -> Plan`

*method*

`Variants::plan`: glyph order, deduplication and locl routing as a Plan
dict `{glyphs: [(name, glyph)], cmap, gsub}`.

#### `fontpixel.variants.Variants.prepare(limits: LayoutLimits | None = ...) -> PreparedVariants`

*method*

`Variants::prepare`: validate and plan once for repeated exports.

Plans an owned copy of the model (Rust borrows it instead), so the
returned handle is independent of later edits to this one.

#### `fontpixel.variants.Variants.retained_usage(max_bytes: int) -> int`

*method*

`Variants::retained_usage`: retained bytes as an owning caller charges
them; raises `ResourceLimitError` above `max_bytes`.

#### `fontpixel.variants.Variants.scripts: list[ScriptVariantItem]`

*property* -- Script alternatives as `[{scripts, font}]`.

#### `fontpixel.variants.Variants.to_dict() -> VariantsDict`

*method* -- The serde Variants dict (fonts as font dicts).

### `fontpixel.variants.defaults() -> VariantsDefaults`

*function* -- Default option dicts of `fontpixel.variants`.

### `fontpixel.variants.encode(variants: Variants, options: ExportOptions | None = ...) -> EncodedFont`

*function* -- `variants::encode`: plan and export a `Variants` handle.

### `fontpixel.variants.encode_single(font: FontLike, options: ExportOptions | None = ...) -> EncodedFont`

*function* -- `variants::encode_single`: export one face without alternatives.

### `fontpixel.variants.encode_single_owned(font: FontLike, options: ExportOptions | None = ...) -> EncodedFont`

*function*

`variants::encode_single_owned`: as `encode_single`, letting the export
own (and drop early) a copy of the face; output is identical.

### `fontpixel.variants.language_tag(value: str) -> str`

*function*

`variants::language_tag`: the OpenType language-system tag of a BCP-47 or
OpenType tag via the OpenType language registry (e.g. `"zh-HK"` → `"ZHH "`);
unknown tags raise `InvalidInputError`.

### `fontpixel.variants.notdef_empty_metrics(policy: NotdefPolicy) -> tuple[int, int] | None`

*function*

`NotdefPolicy::empty_metrics`: `(advance, left_side_bearing)` of an empty
`.notdef` policy, or `None` for `"preserve"`.

### `fontpixel.variants.script_tag(value: str) -> str`

*function*

`variants::script_tag`: validate an explicit four-letter script tag
(e.g. `"latn"`); other lengths or characters raise `InvalidInputError`.

### `fontpixel.variants.validate_metadata(metadata: MetadataOptions, flavor: OutlineFlavor, shape: Shape) -> None`

*function*

`MetadataOptions::validate`: check metadata controls against an outline
`flavor` (`"true_type"`/`"cff"`) and `shape`.

## fontpixel.woff

Bounded standalone sfnt <-> WOFF1/WOFF2 containers.

### `fontpixel.woff.defaults() -> WoffDefaults`

*function* -- Default limit and option dicts of `fontpixel.woff`.

## fontpixel.woff.woff1

WOFF 1.0 (zlib).

### `fontpixel.woff.woff1.decode(data: Buffer | Sequence[int], limits: WoffLimits | None = ...) -> WoffDecoded`

*function* -- `woff1::decode`: reconstruct the standalone sfnt from WOFF1 bytes.

### `fontpixel.woff.woff1.encode(data: Buffer | Sequence[int], options: Woff1Options | None = ..., limits: WoffLimits | None = ...) -> EncodedFont`

*function* -- `woff1::encode`: deterministic WOFF1 of a standalone sfnt.

## fontpixel.woff.woff2

WOFF 2.0 (Brotli, glyf/loca/hmtx transforms, collections).

### `fontpixel.woff.woff2.brotli_encoder_heap_bound(quality: int, lgwin: int, input_len: int, threads: int) -> int | None`

*function*

`woff2::brotli_encoder_heap_bound`: the admitted Brotli encoder heap bound
(proven for quality 0-9, an empirical envelope for 10-11), or `None` on
arithmetic overflow. WOFF2 always uses `lgwin = 22`.

### `fontpixel.woff.woff2.brotli_encoder_proven_heap_bound(quality: int, lgwin: int, input_len: int, threads: int) -> int | None`

*function*

`woff2::brotli_encoder_proven_heap_bound`: the source-derived upper bound
of all encoder heap for the same call shape, or `None` on overflow.

### `fontpixel.woff.woff2.decode(data: Buffer | Sequence[int], limits: WoffLimits | None = ...) -> WoffDecoded`

*function* -- `woff2::decode`: reconstruct the sfnt (or `ttcf` collection) from WOFF2.

### `fontpixel.woff.woff2.encode(data: Buffer | Sequence[int], options: Woff2Options | None = ..., limits: WoffLimits | None = ...) -> EncodedFont`

*function* -- `woff2::encode`: deterministic WOFF2 of an sfnt or `ttcf` collection.

### `fontpixel.woff.woff2.encode_many(inputs: Sequence[Buffer], options: Woff2Options | None = ..., limits: WoffLimits | None = ..., jobs: int = ...) -> list[EncodedFont]`

*function*

`woff2::encode_many`: encode several fonts with up to `jobs` worker
threads (bounded by `max_batch_fonts`/`max_batch_bytes`); output order
matches input order.
